title: Human–AI Loop with Gemini 4 Argon Breaks High-Degree Barrier in Lehmer’s Problem
whyItMatters: Used a Gemini 4 Argon human–AI discovery loop to shatter 100% of prior high-degree Mahler-measure records (d ≥ 166 up to d = 2,000) and uncover a 2D Coulomb-gas root law.
summary: Combining internal Gemini 4 Argon reasoning with exact arithmetic verification, researchers generalized Boyd’s algorithm and broke the high-degree computational barrier in Lehmer’s 1933 Mahler-measure problem across all 996 even degrees d ∈ [10, 2000], surpassing every prior record for d ≥ 166. Interpreting log M(P) as a 2D Coulomb gas potential, exact rational root counting revealed a scale-invariant fraction (~82.5%) of roots on the unit circle.
technicalHighlights: Surpassed 100% of previously known minimal Mahler-measure records for all even degrees d ≥ 166 up to d = 2,000.
Released a complete exact-arithmetic verified benchmark dataset across all 996 even degrees in expanded and cyclotomic-quotient forms.
Uncovered a physical 2D Coulomb-gas interpretation explaining the universal ~82.5% unit-circle root fraction.
caveats: Does not resolve Lehmer’s conjecture itself (whether a uniform lower bound > 1 exists), and the preprint awaits formal journal peer review.

scoreRationale.foundational: Substantially advanced a 93-year-old number-theory problem and revealed new structural root physics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrates the power of tight human–AI algorithmic loops paired with exact rational arithmetic certificates.
scoreRationale.verification: All 996 degree records are verified in exact rational arithmetic over ℚ; preprint under review.
scoreRationale.velocity: Swept through nearly 1,000 polynomial degrees that resisted classical numerical search for decades.
